name: HubSpot
tagline: Build a HubSpot app with the CLI and plug it into Composio. No review up to 25 installs; past that, list it on the Marketplace.

approvalWait.asStated: Marketplace listing: initial review within 10 business days; whole review no more than 60 days from first feedback.

cost.asStated: Free developer account; no paid subscription needed to build apps. No listing fee in the docs we read.

steps.title: Get a HubSpot account and the CLI
instructions: No HubSpot account yet? Create a free one with the sign-up link below.
Install the latest HubSpot CLI. Docs recommend 8.16.0 or later.
Run hs account auth. Generate a Personal Access Key (Development → Keys) when prompted and paste it in.
Your HubSpot user needs Developer tools access to upload projects.
steps.agentTask: Install the HubSpot CLI and check its version. I'll paste the Personal Access Key myself when hs account auth asks.

snippets.code:
npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest
hs --version
hs account auth

warnings.text: Apps are now built as CLI projects. New legacy public apps (Development → Legacy Apps) can't be created since June 23, 2026.

problems.q: Composio's HubSpot page says Apps → Create App
a: That describes legacy public apps, which HubSpot no longer lets you create.
Use the CLI project flow in this guide instead.

steps.title: Create the app project
instructions: Run hs project create and pick App as the base contents.
Distribution: pick Marketplace unless every customer's HubSpot account is one your own HubSpot user can access.
Auth: pick OAuth. A static token installs in one account only.
Features: pick only what you'll build. Composio needs none of them.
In app-hsmeta.json, set uid to a unique name before the first upload. Changing it later creates a new component.

fields.label: Distribution
fields.hint: Up to 25 installs before listing. Private: 10 allowlisted accounts (100 for Solutions Partners)

warnings.text: Private apps only allowlist accounts your HubSpot user already has access to. Most SaaS customers' accounts won't be on that list.
You can switch a private app to marketplace distribution later without interrupting existing installs.

steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run hs project create, so we couldn't see whether it accepts zero features. If not, pick one you can leave unused.

problems.q: hs project create fails or offers no App option
a: Your CLI is probably old. Run npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest and try again.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and scopes
instructions: In app-hsmeta.json, under config.auth, replace redirectUrls with the Composio callback below.
Set requiredScopes to oauth only. Put tool scopes in optionalScopes.
Add only scopes your tools use. Listed apps must use every scope they request.
Run hs project upload to build and deploy the change.
steps.agentTask: Edit app-hsmeta.json: Composio callback in redirectUrls, oauth in requiredScopes, my tools' scopes in optionalScopes. Then hs project upload.

fields.label: redirectUrls
fields.hint: HTTPS required; only http://localhost is exempt

fields.label: requiredScopes
fields.hint: Same list goes in Composio's scopes field

fields.label: optionalScopes (starter)
fields.value: crm.objects.contacts.read crm.objects.contacts.write crm.objects.companies.read crm.objects.companies.write crm.objects.deals.read crm.objects.deals.write crm.objects.owners.read
fields.hint: Same list goes in Composio's optional_scopes field. Trim to your tools

warnings.text: Tokens carry the app's scopes, not the connecting user's HubSpot permissions. Your agent can see more than that user can.
Optional scopes are silently dropped when the account lacks that tool. Tools needing them then fail.

problems.q: Authorization failed because the provided scopes are insufficient
a: A scope in requiredScopes wasn't in the request's scope list.
Put every requiredScopes entry in Composio's scopes field, not optional_scopes.

problems.q: Mismatch between the scopes in the install URL and the app's scopes
a: Composio asked for a scope your app doesn't list, or in the wrong category.
Required in HubSpot → Composio scopes. Optional in HubSpot → Composio optional_scopes. Then upload and reconnect.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
instructions: Run hs project open, or go to Development → Projects and click your project.
Under Project Components, click your app, then open the Auth tab.
Under Client credentials, copy the Client ID and Client secret.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.

problems.q: The secret leaked or I need a new one
a: On the Auth tab, click Rotate next to the client secret, type your app's name, then Rotate secret.
The old secret stops working. Paste the new one into your Composio auth config and reconnect affected accounts.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the HubSpot toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Choose OAuth2, not API key, and turn on your own developer credentials.
Paste your Client ID and Client secret.
Copy requiredScopes into scopes and optionalScopes into optional_scopes, exactly.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Base URL
fields.hint: Per Composio's HubSpot setup page, if the field is shown

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the HubSpot toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick HubSpot, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for hubspot.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Marketplace app: on the app's Distribution tab click Begin publishing and sign the Acceptable Use Policy.
Private app: on the Distribution tab, Add approved account(s) and tick the account you'll test with.
Start a connection for a test user, open the link and pick the HubSpot account.
HubSpot warns the app is unverified. Type I accept the risk, then Connect. Expected until listed.
Developer test accounts don't count toward install limits. Use one to save installs.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. Unverified: whether your own account can connect before Begin publishing or allowlisting.

problems.q: You don't have permission to connect this integration
a: The HubSpot user lacks App Marketplace access or a permission your scopes need, often Edit property settings.
A Super Admin grants it, or connects as Super Admin.

problems.q: This account doesn't have access to some HubSpot features
a: The account's subscription lacks a tool behind one of your required scopes.
Move that scope to optionalScopes and optional_scopes, upload, and reconnect.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: A tool fails with a missing scope
a: The scope was optional and the account didn't grant it, or it's not in your app.
Add it in app-hsmeta.json and the auth config, upload, then have the user reconnect.

steps.title: Let customers install it
instructions: Marketplace app: any HubSpot account can connect, up to 25 installs. Developer test accounts don't count.
Private app: add each customer account under Distribution → Add approved account(s). Cap is 10.
Solutions Partners get 100 private installs, OAuth apps only.
Track installs on the Distribution tab. Past 25 marketplace installs you must be listed.

problems.q: A customer's account isn't in the allowlist picker
a: The picker only lists accounts your HubSpot user can access.
Get user access to their account, or switch the app to marketplace distribution.

problems.q: Can HubSpot raise the 25-install cap before listing?
a: HubSpot's changelog says listing approval removes the cap. It names no other way.

steps.title: Super Admin approves the app
steps.when: When a non-admin user in a customer's HubSpot account hits Request approval.
instructions: Non-admin users must request access to apps their account hasn't approved.
A Super Admin opens Settings → Integrations → Connected Apps → Approved apps → Approve apps.
They pick your app, choose who can install it, review data permissions, then Approve app.
The user then connects again from your product.

problems.q: The admin can't find the Approve apps button
a: Only Super Admins can approve apps. Ask a Super Admin in that account.

steps.title: Meet the listing requirements
steps.when: Only for more than 25 installs or a Marketplace listing. Marketplace distribution only.
instructions: Get at least 3 active installs: unaffiliated production accounts with API activity in the last 30 days.
Use OAuth as the only auth method and use every scope you request.
Publish setup docs specific to this integration, plus live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs.
Add at least one support contact, an install button URL, and pricing that matches your website.
Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement. Submit one app at a time.

warnings.text: Apps where an AI picks CRM actions must enforce user-level permissions. Standard OAuth tokens aren't enough.
User-level access (isUserLevel: true) needs a new app on platform 2026.09. Existing account-level apps can't be migrated.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't confirm Composio connections work with an isUserLevel app, or how HubSpot classifies a Composio-backed agent.

problems.q: My second app submission was rejected immediately
a: HubSpot reviews one app at a time and auto-rejects apps submitted while another is in review.

steps.title: Draft setup docs and listing copy
steps.when: Before you submit a Marketplace listing.
instructions: Draft a public setup guide for this integration: install, connect, disconnect.
List the data you read and write so it matches your requested scopes.
Check every listing URL is live and public. HubSpot crawls them.

steps.title: Wait for listing review
steps.when: After you submit your Marketplace listing.
instructions: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing by hand.
Answer feedback quickly. The whole process should end within 60 days of first feedback.
Once approved, HubSpot removes the 25-install cap automatically.

wait.asStated: Initial review within 10 business days; whole review no more than 60 days from the time feedback is shared.
